label: token right after an early k (input steps 1-2)
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase on the step right after a k, but only when that k is original token 0 or 1 (so t = 1 or 2). The token at the firing step does not matter. On dev the predicate has precision 1.0 and covers 99.9% of activation mass. Magnitude: strongest at t=1, after k as the first token (about 1.0 of max, 4.1). At t=2 it is weaker, about 0.5-0.66 of max when k is the second token after some other first token. It is higher (about 0.8-1.0) when the sequence starts with k. It does not fire after a k later in the sequence (t>=3 adds false positives), in the delimiter or copy phases, or on the k itself. The steps the predicate misses (about 1/3 of active steps) carry only about 0.1% of the mass. They are near-zero activations at t=1-2 after w, y or v.

issues: Count recall is only 0.683 (test), but the missed steps (15560 on test) carry 0.1% of the mass. Every miss shown is about 0.00 of max at t=1 after w, y or v, so they are near-threshold noise, as the explanation says. Activation-quartile coverage on test is 0 / 0.73 / 1.0 / 1.0, so all misses are in the bottom half.
Small residual: at t=3 right after a 'k k' prefix (e.g. s k [k] [1:0.04]) there are weak tails of up to about 0.16. On dev, t=3 with prev=k has precision 0.034 and mass 0.1%. This is negligible.

Magnitude claims hold. Mean activation per step at t=2 is about 0.62x that at t=1. For t=2 when first_tok==k (k k _), it is about 0.81x t=1. Both match 'weaker 0.5-0.66' and 'higher 0.8-1.0 when the sequence starts with k'.

The phase claims hold. Delimiter has 2 active steps and copy has 143 (dev), with about 0 mass. t=0 is never active. When in_tok==k at t=1 it fires only if prev is also k. The precision of 0.68 for a t<=3 window is consistent with the counts.
